reference.source: Reconstruction version 6, right MANO wrist, plug_white world pose, phase annotations and object-frame contact witnesses.
reference.kinematic_replay: Align the opening blade direction to deployment yaw about the tabletop normal. Offset to the fixed start and gradually bring the endpoint to the center of the goal. Apply measured wrist rotations relative to the grasp wrist, which is anchored in the reachable robot hand frame from an opposed thumb–middle-finger pad solve. Re-solve the pad locations and the arm IK per frame. Choose the smallest collision-clear separation available at each frame. Keep the measured plug trajectory as an imposed pose for the kinematic audit.
reference.planned_reward_reference: Adapt the demonstrated object and wrist traces to each start and goal. Use object position, blade-axis rotation, wrist tracking, opposed-contact witnesses and ordered state-dependent progress. Keep the reconstruction in the reward and curriculum.

arm.controller: Public 100 Hz palm jump test, linear and rotational slew, box clamp, measured-joint seeded IK, coupled wrist and command speed clamps. Delayed position reference followed by an implicit, current-limited arm joint servo. Command and measured capsules are evaluated each tick.
arm.numerical_limit: The public reference integrator occasionally advances its feed-forward component past the IK boundary. Project the resulting joint reference to the same joint and coupled wrist box and clear outward velocity at a projected joint, consistent with the published lack of boundary overshoot. The unreachable-orientation test then passes.

hand.controller: Five ordered four-joint digits, 2 Hz first-order filter, 25 ms nominal fractional delay, torque-limited implicit position servo and compliant joint stops. Measured hand positions are delayed and receive 0.10 degree encoder noise.
hand.domain_randomization: Draw nominal or randomized strength, delay, friction, object inertia/mass, table edges and stop compliance. Nominal values are used in the frozen evaluation. The sampled distributions for each training run are recorded with its iteration.

sensor.source: Published d2s_sensor.PoseSensor for delay, symmetry flips, noise, loss and validity/age. Contact-mesh-derived capsules approximate ego occlusion; sample 112 physical housing surface points and 12 blade face points. Recompute visibility at each physics-log tick.
sensor.encoder_delay: Normal 14 ms with 4.3 ms deviation, clipped to 4–29 ms and sampled on the logged 100 Hz trajectory.

initial_conditions.object: Uniform and independent xy offsets ±10 mm, yaw offset ±10 degrees about -90 degrees, state +X upward. Place with zero velocities on the table and verify support with the installed hold check. Use the published start IK and 1.5 s hand ramp.

episode.termination: Published geometric and jump stops and invalid action or nonfinite state as policy failure. Finger and arm travel violations are logged without turning contact force into a stop.

station_check.departure: Index MCP1 encoder finite-difference peak 10.11 rad/s versus the model sheet 8.203 rad/s and the filtered-step bound 22.12 rad/s. The documents leave this measurement interpretation open. There is no measured excursion outside the allowed travel in the scenario.

validation.fk: Compared MuJoCo palm FK to the arm model at reset (about 4 micrometres); station adapter passes published free-space, limit and stop checks.
validation.sensor_replay: One complete 900-step hold episode independently matches d2s_measures contract validation with zero violations. The seed used for the local hold is 1604. The gate will replay the sensor on candidate episodes.
validation.initial_hold: The installed support checker passes the reset-finger start. Palm drift rounds to 0.0 mm, maximum finger change 0.003 rad and object remains supported.
validation.rollout_penetration: The evaluator measures the deepest signed contact distance in every rollout. Physical task feasibility remains to be established.
limitations: Mass, friction and inertia remain priors pending target calibration. Geometry treats blade holes and rear electrical recess as closed collision surfaces.

body.text: In baseline r0019 every rollout lifted the plug. Its two selected failure videos were reproduced locally with the harness renderer because the gate render sandbox had no saved states. At 2.2–4.3 s the housing rolls down under the thumb and middle while their spacing changes little. Seed 2105443589 accumulates 31 degrees of passive displacement, and 610157588 accumulates 49.1 degrees under the standard measure. I will prioritize continuous pad travel planned from the measured lifted grasp and stabilize before translating. A local adaptive probe on seed 5 completed the full sequence with 74.2 degrees total opposed rotation, 5.6 degrees passive, and a supported upright seat. I will check the same dynamics and thresholds on diverse starts before treating that as proof.

The raw deployment-heading transfer put the demonstration wrist on the far side of the plug. I aligned its relative wrist stroke to the reachable thumb–middle grasp anchor of simulation record r0012. Reach checks on two starts had at least 22.5 mm station clearance during the tracked grasp. The resulting wrist reference is soft, since the robot has longer digits and a different approach. For a later scratch PPO curriculum, generated intermediate poses are settled in simulation after their temporary clamp fixture is removed. The training start pool contains positions, velocities and static preload only. Controller actions and trajectories will not enter the network, its loss or its output. Hold and random-action reward sanity checks are being run in the exact station while the feasibility proof is pending.

body.reflection: Same scratch PPO actor and training curves as r0024. The only policy change is the fixed pose output range. Relative target integration exceeded the reachability tracking envelope on every r0026 trial. The bounded action representation passed all of the gate r0028 contract checks and became the first task incumbent. Fixed-start lifts 29/64, five measured finger travel violations, zero stops and no qualifying turns or placements. Gate results 14/32 lifts, five violations, no stops or qualifying turns. Final arm and finger rest improved to 12/64 fixed starts. Target round s01 submitted under gate r0028 to determine if the initial opposed lift transfers and where contact is lost.

body.text: r0028 passed the contract and became incumbent, with 14 lifts, five measured finger violations, no stops and no successful turn. Its frozen v2 renderer failed because archived state logs were not in the render sandbox. I opened right montages of both selected failure placements, 2016753880 and 1906705580, re-rendered locally with independent sensor noise. They touched around 0.18 s, briefly opposed the housing, and lost it while the wrist swept up at 0.60–0.69 s. Their clearance maxima were 0.7 and 12.2 mm, and neither sustained opposed lift. On 128 matched placements the delivered actor lifted 65 on CPU and 29 on GPU, with 77 vs 33 durable-lift drops, so the current GPU port fails outcome parity on the moving actor. The weaker midpoint passed only with zero sustained holds. On 20 archived CPU lifts, Warp lifted 7 with the original box table, 10 with its finite convex hull, and 6 with a plane. This is a diagnostic and no model change is adopted. The CPU and GPU state-level check showed six percent contact-set mismatch concentrated in box–mesh contact, zero mesh–mesh count differences, and no buffer overflow. R1 was delivered on time. I will use target judgments and sent-command replays before choosing which contact or control quantities to calibrate.

The full 30 Hz MuJoCo Warp station, with 2 ms physics, 100 Hz arm and hand controllers, geometric stops and the published batched pose sensor, sustained 149,824 aggregate environment steps per second across four L40S GPUs with 2,048 worlds each during a hold benchmark. All four ranks reported zero stops, zero hardware violations and zero contact-buffer overflows. The PPO port ran one smoke update with 10,637 samples and KL 0.017. I have not started long training. The active incumbent still fails CPU–GPU grasp-outcome parity, and an isolated throughput number does not settle that difference. In diagnostic sixteen-start command replays, 15 ms finger delay improved the sustained-hold count on both table geometries; this is a parameter-sensitivity result and has not been applied to the simulator.

The current incumbent passed paired outcome parity over 128 starts when the GPU deployment start used the settled robot state, delay histories and previously measured joint state from the exact CPU ramp. The GPU still simulated the 1.5 s scene ramp and pose sensor, and the next 30 seconds of full station dynamics. The common CPU ramp has no hand–plug contact, so it uses the same mechanically initialized arm and hand for every compatible start. Compared with the CPU, GPU lifts were 72 versus 65, durable-lift drops 78 versus 77, hardware violations 22 versus 14, and success zero on both. All three official outcome tolerances passed. A smaller open-loop diagnostic moved from 7 to 14 sustained holds against 16 on CPU. This shows the pre-roll configuration is a major source of the contact mismatch. A repeat with an independent GPU sensor-noise stream is running. This option is diagnostic until R1 judgment and command replay are complete.

trials.evidence: The front-right and head-camera views show the housing rocking against the fingers and lying blade-horizontal on the table by file time 2.33 s. The observed centre rose at most 6.8 mm on valid estimator rows, with a gap from policy time 0.30 to 2.73 s during contact. Continuous opposed lift and active in-hand turn were unverified. Over the final half-second the valid pose has median y = -0.171 m and blade tilt 89.8 degrees. The palm range was 16.0 mm. The middle MCP1 measured 0.071 rad beyond its deployed limit.

The head view briefly shows a blade above the fingers and the front-right view shows the plug skidding forward before the hand rises away. The estimator is invalid from 0.30 to 2.73 s, so the logs cannot establish an opposed unsupported hold. The final medians are x = 0.652 m, y = -0.182 m and blade tilt 89.8 degrees. The palm range was 12.4 mm and middle MCP1 exceeded its limit by 0.053 rad.

The operator marked a turn. In the front-right view the housing briefly tips next to the flexing fingers around file time 1.91–2.08 s, then separates and lies on its side by 2.33 s. Estimator dropout from 0.30 to 2.80 s covers that interval. I could not establish 0.10 s of opposed lift or the 38-degree hand-relative active turn within the same unsupported grasp. The plug ends at x = 0.629 m, y = -0.252 m and 90.5 degrees tilt. The final palm moves 6.9 mm and pinky MCP1 exceeds its limit by 0.042 rad.

The front-right view shows the housing tilting briefly against the fingertips at file time 1.91 s and falling back as the wrist leaves. Estimator dropout 0.30–2.47 s prevents measuring maintained opposition or clearance. It finishes close to the start, y = -0.207 m and blade tilt 90.0 degrees, with final palm range 5.6 mm. Index MCP1 exceeded its limit by 0.048 rad.

The operator marked a turn. The front-right view shows a momentary tip at file time 1.91 s followed by separation and an on-table slide. The active turn threshold cannot be established through the estimator gap at policy time 0.30–2.47 s or from the visible contact. The hand withdraws without a held carry. Final medians x = 0.590 m, y = -0.191 m and tilt 89.6 degrees fail the placement condition. Final palm range was 9.5 mm and index DIP exceeded its limit by 0.025 rad.

The front-right view shows the fingers pressing the plug and it leaving their reach along the table by file time 2.33 s. Pose loss at 0.27–2.43 s leaves no continuous estimator record of the contact. There is no sustained opposed lift in the video. The estimated plug finishes at x = 0.617 m, y = -0.150 m and tilt 89.8 degrees. Final palm range was 8.3 mm and index MCP1 exceeded its limit by 0.037 rad.

The head and front-right views show a small rock then separation with the housing still on the right. The last valid heading before loss reaches 80.6 degrees from up at 0.30 s, with 4.3 mm maximum observed body rise. Estimator loss 0.33–2.50 s and the videos do not establish sustained opposed motion. The plug finishes at y = -0.174 m and tilt 89.7 degrees. Final palm range 9.7 mm and middle MCP2 excursion 0.058 rad beyond its limit also fail criteria.

The plug skids from under the palm and remains on its side after the hand rises in the front-right view. The estimator is invalid at policy time 0.30–2.50 s, and the video gives no continuous opposed lift or carry. The plug ends at y = -0.145 m and tilt 89.8 degrees. Final palm range was 6.3 mm and index MCP1 crossed its deployed limit by 0.054 rad.

body.next: The first visible failure is loss of stable opposing contact before a sustained lift. Replay the sent commands and test whether delayed arm motion, finger lag or excessive compliant-stop travel explain why the simulator sometimes lifted under this policy. Measure pose loss separately from physical displacement. Use the reproduced dynamics to guide the next PPO continuation.

body.observation_mismatch: Opened the head and both substitute camera views for every trial. The target tracker lost the plug from approximately 0.27–0.33 s until 2.43–2.80 s, including the first grasp attempt. End poses are visible on all eight. The pose at t=0 is the estimator's full-precision first valid measured row. For object residuals I considered only valid rows and treated the stated 180-degree blade-axis symmetry as equivalent. The nominal replay's median of per-trial valid position medians was 334 mm. Median orientation error modulo the stated symmetry was 100 degrees because the plug ended up in a different place and usually on a different face. The outcome mismatch persists after projecting the estimator start to the nominal support face and height. A same-placement re-render for gate r0028 used another sensor stream and was judged as diagnostic only.
body.dynamics_mismatch: I replayed all 900 sent palm and finger commands for each of the eight trials from the package start with the full ramp in simulation version 1. The nominal replays had eight qualifying lifts and no qualifying turns or placements. The target videos and logs establish zero qualifying lifts and zero placements. The measured target arm angles at t=0 match the package start IK exactly. In version 1 repeated palm IK during the finger ramp changed null-space posture by up to 9.53 degrees per joint, despite only 0.99 mm of palm difference. Changing only the initialization to hold the placed arm joints throughout the ramp produced zero simulated lifts. It reduced the median of valid-rows position medians from 334 mm to 53 mm and median peak wrist residual from 51.4 to 49.7 mm. A 105 ms arm delay with the old ramp produced one lift, a 35 ms hand delay produced five, and increasing the finger-stop excursion parameter from 0.002 to 0.006 rad preserved all eight lifts. These alternatives cannot explain the observed initial joint angles. The target finger encoders exceeded the allowance in all eight trials by measured excursions of 0.025–0.071 rad across several fingers. Nominal replay maxima were 0.008–0.018 rad, and the joint-hold alternative reached 0.012–0.025 rad. Target peak external torque had median 89.95 Nm versus 28.03 Nm in the nominal replay and 32.39 Nm in the joint-hold replay. External torque is an observation and the target reported no stops or clips.
body.changes: Use the measured and specified start convention of placing the arm at the start IK joints and holding those joint references through the 1.5 s finger ramp, then start the same 100 Hz Cartesian chain with first command checked against the measured palm. The attached replays are the full original simulation-version-1 baseline. Keep the ramp-matched replays and other no-change controls under work/[redacted]. The ramp hypothesis reproduces the first-stage target outcome and exact initial arm branch. For the remaining discrepancy, examine finger compliance and delay ranges and matching grasp/no-grasp frequencies across them; avoid selecting a parameter from the target's occluded pose alone. Report the increased finger excursions explicitly and use range-aware hardware penalties in subsequent learning after the appropriate gate. The target force model and its lost pose interval limit exact trajectory identification.

reference.source: Reconstruction version 6, right MANO wrist, plug_white world pose, phase annotations and object-frame contact witnesses.
reference.kinematic_replay: Align the opening blade direction to deployment yaw about the tabletop normal. Offset to the fixed start and gradually bring the endpoint to the center of the goal. Apply measured wrist rotations relative to the grasp wrist, which is anchored in the reachable robot hand frame from an opposed thumb–middle-finger pad solve. Re-solve the pad locations and the arm IK per frame. Choose the smallest collision-clear separation available at each frame. Keep the measured plug trajectory as an imposed pose for the kinematic audit.
reference.planned_reward_reference: Adapt the demonstrated object and wrist traces to each start and goal. Use object position, blade-axis rotation, wrist tracking, opposed-contact witnesses and ordered state-dependent progress. Keep the reconstruction in the reward and curriculum.

arm.controller: Public 100 Hz palm jump test, linear and rotational slew, box clamp, measured-joint seeded IK, coupled wrist and command speed clamps. Delayed position reference followed by an implicit, current-limited arm joint servo. Command and measured capsules are evaluated each tick.
arm.numerical_limit: The public reference integrator occasionally advances its feed-forward component past the IK boundary. Project the resulting joint reference to the same joint and coupled wrist box and clear outward velocity at a projected joint, consistent with the published lack of boundary overshoot. The unreachable-orientation test then passes.
arm.initialization_correction: Target replay r0034 showed that re-solving Cartesian IK at the placed palm during the ramp changed the arm null-space posture by 9.53 degrees. Joint hold reproduced all eight observed no-lift outcomes and reduced the median valid-state position residual from 334 mm to 53 mm. The remaining post-start Cartesian and arm servo law is the same.

hand.controller: Five ordered four-joint digits, 2 Hz first-order filter, 25 ms nominal fractional delay, torque-limited implicit position servo and compliant joint stops. Measured hand positions are delayed and receive 0.10 degree encoder noise.
hand.domain_randomization: Draw nominal or randomized strength, delay, friction, object inertia/mass, table edges and stop compliance. Nominal values are used in the frozen evaluation. The sampled distributions for each training run are recorded with its iteration.

sensor.source: Published d2s_sensor.PoseSensor for delay, symmetry flips, noise, loss and validity/age. Contact-mesh-derived capsules approximate ego occlusion; sample 112 physical housing surface points and 12 blade face points. Recompute visibility at each physics-log tick.
sensor.encoder_delay: Normal 14 ms with 4.3 ms deviation, clipped to 4–29 ms and sampled on the logged 100 Hz trajectory.
sensor.training_backend: Published TorchPoseSensorBatch with the same default noise, delays and occlusion schedule, using the same 124 samples and arm or hand capsule rays in Warp. CPU and GPU use independently seeded noise streams.

initial_conditions.object: Uniform and independent xy offsets ±10 mm, yaw offset ±10 degrees about -90 degrees, state +X upward. Place with zero velocities on the table and verify support with the installed hold check. Use the published start IK and 1.5 s hand ramp.
initial_conditions.arm_ramp: Solve the package start once from the published reset joints. Keep those placed joint references for all 150 finger ramp ticks while gravity, finger dynamics, collisions and the pose sensor advance. No Cartesian IK iterations run the warm arm reference. At t=0, compare the first action with the measured palm. Local arm variation was at most 2.18e-5 rad over the ramp, and the final joint vector differs from target [redacted] by at most 1.63e-6 rad.
initial_conditions.training: GPU PPO uses the same simulated 1.5-second deployment ramp on each complete reset. Optional intermediate-state starts restore the position, velocity and hand preload of a mechanically settled pose. The fixture used during offline initialization is gone before the saved states. No controller commands enter the network training targets.

episode.termination: Published geometric and jump stops and invalid action or nonfinite state as policy failure. Finger and arm travel violations are logged without turning contact force into a stop.

station_check.departure: Index MCP1 finite-difference peak 10.105 rad/s on CPU and 10.106 on GPU, above the 8.203 rad/s model value and below the public 2 Hz-filtered-step limit 22.117 rad/s. No stop or measured excess travel in the check. The hardware spec leaves the interpretation of the quantized peak open.

validation.fk: Compared MuJoCo palm FK to the arm model at reset (about 4 micrometres); station adapter passes published free-space, limit and stop checks.
validation.sensor_replay: Four independent 900-step lock-ramp candidate state logs reproduced contract-v3 sensor observations and all other checks with zero discrepancies.
validation.initial_hold: All 128 deployment evaluations retained the intended joint hold during the finger ramp and started the actor without a station stop. A full gate start check on the frozen v3 evaluator will verify the support convention.
validation.rollout_penetration: Kinematic reference maximum 0.992 mm. The maximum signed hand–plug overlap on the 128 CPU corrected-ramp neural rollouts is 3.88 mm. Early impacts can press the current estimated compliance more deeply than the kinematic replay. The current actor is a baseline and poses a finger travel risk in contact.
limitations: Mass, friction and inertia remain priors pending target calibration. Geometry treats blade holes and rear electrical recess as closed collision surfaces.

Capsules approximate partial occlusion by the glove. Finger pads are compliant contact surfaces over rigid links. The kinematic replay deviates up to 32 mm from the unconstrained palm placement and comes within 5 mm of the plug in 50 of 76 grasp frames. The reconstruction wrist and object remain the demonstration targets.

The target, nominal replay and corrected replay had median per-trial peak external torques of 89.95, 28.03 and 32.39 Nm. This is an estimated observation. Target finger excursions beyond the deployed travel allowance occurred in eight of eight; the corrected sent-command replay reproduced them in three of eight. Continue calibration using outcomes and uncertainty, not exact occluded trajectories.

They do not establish parity through the complete skill. Earlier contact-rich same-command diagnostics and old-ramp same-policy comparisons remain separate evidence.

validation.target_replay: r0033 judgment and r0034 nominal open-loop replay, with controlled joint-hold hypothesis archived in target_replay_diagnostic.json. The simulator still underestimates some finger excursions and torque. The object pose is only compared on valid estimator rows.

body.reason: Freeze exactly the same corrected station, evaluator, stages, constraints and sampler as task suite v3. Simulation version 2 matches the target arm joint hold during the finger ramp. The renderer now rebuilds missing selected rollouts.
body.gate_evidence: r0028: the two local right views showed shallow loss of grip and the gate renderer had no state files. Target replay r0034 identified the null-space shift during the original warmup, which the new CPU and GPU joint hold removes.
body.warning: suite plug-feasibility version 2's incumbent r0022 meets its pass rate (success 19/32 = 0.594 >= 0.25). Version 3 starts over: its first gate is a new baseline, and the suite loses its standing until version 3's incumbent meets its pass rate (another suite of the link that meets its own still counts). Tightening your own criteria resets what you have proven; do it only for a reason the demonstration or the task gives, and say it in --reason (demo2sim/VERIFICATION.md section 3).

body.text: After correcting the initial arm hold, the R1 replay still showed compliant finger excursions over 0.02 rad in only 3/8 of the eight trials, versus 8/8 measured on the target. A controlled replay with 0.006 rad stop compliance reproduced 8/8 excursions between 0.027 and 0.034 rad. The published 0.010 rad upper bound reproduced 8/8 between 0.034 and 0.048 rad. Both kept zero qualifying lifts, matching the videos. Changing only grip scale to 0.85 reproduced zero excursions and zero lifts. The measured target range 0.025–0.071 rad argues for spanning the full plausible compliance range in training. The torque gap persists. Leave the frozen nominal judge and its thresholds intact; test a wider 0.001–0.010 rad training distribution, along with the existing randomized mass, friction, table extent and time constants.

scene.robot: Complete supplied Marvin–Wuji MJCF with official arm capsules and hand collision meshes, the parked left arm and the column and head stop volumes. Added table, pedestal and floor. The geometric station stops are evaluated directly on commanded and measured arm angles.

object_physical_properties.dominant_material: molded thermoplastic housing, plated metal blades

sources.mass_kg: Comparable Anker and Belkin 20 W adapters span 36–52 g (https://www.anker.com/products/b2348112-f0 and https://www.belkin.com/support-article/?articleNum=337529). Adopt 51 g for the larger housing.
sources.com_m: Homogeneous housing with heavier internal assembly offset 2 mm toward the back and two exterior brass blade cuboids.
sources.inertia_com_kgm2: Parallel-axis combination of housing and blade cuboids about the inferred combined COM.
sources.friction: Assumed effective coefficients for molded polymer against smooth laminate. Measure and randomize for robot deployment.
sources.restitution: Assumed 0.05, weak bounce of molded plastic on a rigid table; not identifiable from the clip.
sources.dominant_material: Appearance and construction class suggest a stiff molded thermoplastic with plated metal blades. Resin and alloy unobservable.
sources.size_m: TASK_CONFIG.md section 3 dimensions for the visually matching station adapter. Industrial design is consistent with the white Type A Apple 20 W USB-C form in https://www.apple.com/shop/product/mwvv3am/a/20w-usb-c-power-adapter. Brand identity is unconfirmed.

reference.source: Reconstruction version 6, right MANO wrist, plug_white world pose, phase annotations and object-frame contact witnesses.
reference.kinematic_replay: Align the opening blade direction to deployment yaw about the tabletop normal. Offset to the fixed start and gradually bring the endpoint to the center of the goal. Apply measured wrist rotations relative to the grasp wrist, which is anchored in the reachable robot hand frame from an opposed thumb–middle-finger pad solve. Re-solve the pad locations and the arm IK per frame. Choose the smallest collision-clear separation available at each frame. Keep the measured plug trajectory as an imposed pose for the kinematic audit.
reference.planned_reward_reference: Adapt the demonstrated object and wrist traces to each start and goal. Use object position, blade-axis rotation, wrist tracking, opposed-contact witnesses and ordered state-dependent progress. Keep the reconstruction in the reward and curriculum.

arm.controller: Public 100 Hz palm jump test, linear and rotational slew, box clamp, measured-joint seeded IK, coupled wrist and command speed clamps. Delayed position reference followed by an implicit, current-limited arm joint servo. Command and measured capsules are evaluated each tick.
arm.numerical_limit: The public reference integrator occasionally advances its feed-forward component past the IK boundary. Project the resulting joint reference to the same joint and coupled wrist box and clear outward velocity at a projected joint, consistent with the published lack of boundary overshoot. The unreachable-orientation test then passes.
arm.initialization_correction: Target replay r0034 showed that re-solving Cartesian IK at the placed palm during the ramp changed the arm null-space posture by 9.53 degrees. Joint hold reproduced all eight observed no-lift outcomes and reduced the median valid-state position residual from 334 mm to 53 mm. The remaining post-start Cartesian and arm servo law is the same.

hand.controller: Five ordered four-joint digits, 2 Hz first-order filter, 25 ms nominal fractional delay, torque-limited implicit position servo and compliant joint stops. Measured hand positions are delayed and receive 0.10 degree encoder noise.
hand.domain_randomization: Draw nominal or randomized strength, delay, friction, object inertia/mass, table edges and stop compliance. Nominal values are used in the frozen evaluation. The sampled distributions for each training run are recorded with its iteration.
hand.stop_distributions: Use .001–.010 rad sampled uniformly on randomized episodes, converted to max(.004, .006 × sqrt(compliance/.002)) for the constraint time constant while retaining the nominal damping ratio and deployed limits. The nominal compliant-stop setting remains .002 rad.

sensor.source: Published d2s_sensor.PoseSensor for delay, symmetry flips, noise, loss and validity/age. Contact-mesh-derived capsules approximate ego occlusion; sample 112 physical housing surface points and 12 blade face points. Recompute visibility at each physics-log tick.
sensor.encoder_delay: Normal 14 ms with 4.3 ms deviation, clipped to 4–29 ms and sampled on the logged 100 Hz trajectory.
sensor.training_backend: Published TorchPoseSensorBatch with the same default noise, delays and occlusion schedule, using the same 124 samples and arm or hand capsule rays in Warp. CPU and GPU use independently seeded noise streams.

initial_conditions.object: Uniform and independent xy offsets ±10 mm, yaw offset ±10 degrees about -90 degrees, state +X upward. Place with zero velocities on the table and verify support with the installed hold check. Use the published start IK and 1.5 s hand ramp.
initial_conditions.arm_ramp: Solve the package start once from the published reset joints. Keep those placed joint references for all 150 finger ramp ticks while gravity, finger dynamics, collisions and the pose sensor advance. No Cartesian IK iterations run the warm arm reference. At t=0, compare the first action with the measured palm. Local arm variation was at most 2.18e-5 rad over the ramp, and the final joint vector differs from target [redacted] by at most 1.63e-6 rad.
initial_conditions.training: GPU PPO uses the same simulated 1.5-second deployment ramp on each complete reset. Optional intermediate-state starts restore the position, velocity and hand preload of a mechanically settled pose. The fixture used during offline initialization is gone before the saved states. No controller commands enter the network training targets.

episode.termination: Published geometric and jump stops and invalid action or nonfinite state as policy failure. Finger and arm travel violations are logged without turning contact force into a stop.

station_check.departure: Index MCP1 finite-difference peak 10.105 rad/s on CPU and 10.106 on GPU, above the 8.203 rad/s model value and below the public 2 Hz-filtered-step limit 22.117 rad/s. No stop or measured excess travel in the check. The hardware spec leaves the interpretation of the quantized peak open.

validation.fk: Compared MuJoCo palm FK to the arm model at reset (about 4 micrometres); station adapter passes published free-space, limit and stop checks.
validation.sensor_replay: Four independent 900-step lock-ramp candidate state logs reproduced contract-v3 sensor observations and all other checks with zero discrepancies.
validation.initial_hold: All 128 deployment evaluations retained the intended joint hold during the finger ramp and started the actor without a station stop. A full gate start check on the frozen v3 evaluator will verify the support convention.
validation.rollout_penetration: Kinematic reference maximum 0.992 mm. The maximum signed hand–plug overlap on the 128 CPU corrected-ramp neural rollouts is 3.88 mm. Early impacts can press the current estimated compliance more deeply than the kinematic replay. The current actor is a baseline and poses a finger travel risk in contact.
limitations: Mass, friction and inertia remain priors pending target calibration. Geometry treats blade holes and rear electrical recess as closed collision surfaces.

Capsules approximate partial occlusion by the glove. Finger pads are compliant contact surfaces over rigid links. The kinematic replay deviates up to 32 mm from the unconstrained palm placement and comes within 5 mm of the plug in 50 of 76 grasp frames. The reconstruction wrist and object remain the demonstration targets.

The target, nominal replay and corrected replay had median per-trial peak external torques of 89.95, 28.03 and 32.39 Nm. This is an estimated observation. Target finger excursions beyond the deployed travel allowance occurred in eight of eight; the corrected sent-command replay reproduced them in three of eight. Continue calibration using outcomes and uncertainty, not exact occluded trajectories.

parity.warmstart: Independent 1.5-second physical joint-hold ramps on both nominal backends. GPU batch fields allocated under the randomized model and set to nominal for the paired comparison.
parity.limitation: The corrected CPU and GPU both prevent the old actor from lifting. These paired outcomes establish agreement on initial failed contact and hardware rates. They do not establish parity through the complete skill. Earlier contact-rich same-command diagnostics and old-ramp same-policy comparisons remain separate evidence.

throughput.measurement: All 8,192 worlds use randomized physics. Hold benchmark timed after startup, including sensors and exact control and physics rates, without PPO gradients or reset overhead.

validation.target_replay: r0034 matched R1 no-lift outcomes using joint hold, and r0038 identified compliance as a contributor to encoder excursions. At the nominal setting 3/8 command replays exceeded the allowance, versus 8/8 on target. At compliance variants 0.006 and 0.010 rad, both reproduce 8/8 and no qualifying lifts. The increased range covers the frequency and part of the observed magnitude, with remaining torque and motion errors.
validation.dynamic_contact_diagnostic: Nominal randomized-backend replay of four privileged feasibility command histories. GPU and CPU lifted 4/4. CPU had 4 turns and 3 carries and places. GPU had 2 turns, carries and places, with zero drops, stops, hardware violations or overflows. This compares identical commands without training data or a GPU feasibility policy.

body.text: Feasibility r0040 proves the corrected station: 32/32 lift, 31/32 turn, 23/32 carry, 16/32 place, with zero hardware violations. I opened both hold-out failure and success montages. In seed 69696289 the low supported approach around 6 s ends at an arm collision. In 1059052049 the hand remains just beside an upright plug after the carry missed its measured requirements. The successful trials release into stable upright rest. Continue the r0024 scratch actor, using the exact r0029 geometric output bounds and the reconstructed progression reward, in simulation r0039. The target-supported joint hold and broader physical randomization are the intended changes. Run synchronous PPO with one network across three GPUs for 42 minutes, 6,144 worlds, 80-step rollouts, global 6,144-sample minibatches, and 40 percent physical randomization. The critic head and exploration variance start from their original initialization because the first package saves only its actor weights. I expect the full-start lift rate to increase before the exact hand-relative turn rate. Compare periodic checkpoints on the same CPU 64-start set and use the corrected task baseline for the first paired gate. The 80-step distributed station probe used frozen weights and reached 36,081 active steps per second in its busier batch; neither probe updated a policy.

body.hypothesis: Re-establish the unchanged bounded scratch-PPO incumbent as the baseline for the target-calibrated joint-hold station. R1 and the corrected paired probes predict no qualifying lifts at this baseline.
body.observed: r0028 lift failures showed a briefly opposed plug separating during wrist rise. In r0034 the locked-ramp command replays removed false lifts and reproduced the target first-stage outcome.

body.text: I opened both task v3 baseline failure montages from r0042. At 0.46 s the wrist is already pressing near the plug, with the housing below the fingers. By 4.38 s the palm swings up empty and the plug remains on the tabletop. Gate measures give 0 and 0.62 mm maximum housing clearance for the two reviewed seeds, and zero opposed unsupported time for both. The baseline had 0 lifts, turns, carries or full placements in 32 starts, with two finger travel violations and no stops. The renderer fix produced both montages. The ongoing PPO continuation r0041 must improve the opening grip, and I will compare full starts on the exact CPU process before gating a candidate.

body.reflection: Continuation of the actor trained from scratch in r0024 and using the bounded action map in r0029. The corrected-ramp task baseline r0042 reached no lifts across 32 starts and showed a sweep away from the plug after first contact. The same on-policy reward in simulator v3 uses the R1-derived compliance range and restored mass and table variation. At 12,384,851 new transitions, the checkpoint qualified for lift on 52/64 independent fixed nominal episodes with zero hardware violations or stops, versus 0/128 in the corrected baseline. body.text: The first GPU checkpoint from r0044 became task incumbent r0045. It lifted on 24 of 32 fresh paired starts versus 0 for the previous policy, with 0 versus 3 hardware violations, no stops, and no complete turns. I opened both official turn failure montages. At 0.46 s the object is pinched near the table, and by 4.38 s it is back on the table under an empty hand. Seed 18712140 stayed opposed for 0.47 s, rose 258 mm and reached 19.3 degrees standard hand-relative rotation. Seed 758745650 stayed opposed 0.91 s, rose 288 mm and reached 24.2 degrees. Their minimum blade tilts from upright were 86.7 and 80.0 degrees. Submit this checkpoint for target [redacted] to resolve lift transfer and quantify the subsequent loss. The already planned unchanged PPO run continues while the target runs. Fixed-start diagnostics show the old turn potential awards positive local rotation even when it does not aim the blade upward. A candidate potential conditioned on reduction in world blade tilt would lower median turn credit on these failed first grasps from 0.176 to 0.033, while preserving maximum credit on three of four verified feasibility rollouts from the first valid grasp. Consider it after target judgment/replay and the long-run curve.

body.reflection: Same fully specified PPO run and simulation as r0044. The 24,557,690-step checkpoint lifted on 56/64 of the same nominal starts versus 52/64 at 12.38M, with zero hardware violations and stops in both evaluations. Eight starts lifted only with the later checkpoint and four only with the former (one-sided sign p = 0.194). Qualifying turns and complete task successes remain zero. Later median opposed duration declined from 0.79 to 0.75 s, standard hand-relative rotation among lifted episodes from 28.85 to 19.60 degrees, and peak centre rise from 289 to 249 mm. Final robot rest is 10/64 versus 15/64. Keep the accepted r0045 checkpoint as incumbent. Continue with unchanged training until the planned endpoint because the intermediate full-state start distribution and later learning need more samples.

body.text: I measured the first two GPU checkpoints from the same 16 mechanically prepared states per phase under the CPU sensor model. Among turn starts, advancement rose from 7/16 at r0044 to 11/16 at r0047. The second checkpoint advanced on all five prepared thumb–ring turn starts. Prepared turn clearances are 46–60 mm, while the first full-start checkpoint has a median 167 mm peak clearance during its first opposed grasp and zero full-start turns. Adapted reconstruction r0009 stays between 12 and 36 mm during turn, and successful feasibility r0040 reached at most 52 mm in its reviewed trials. This favors a lift-to-turn transfer problem over a general inability to move the ring finger. If the planned run and target R2 still have no turn, first test a soft excess-clearance reward during the unsupported lift and turn while preserving all other reward terms and policy outputs. Keep the world-direction potential as a separate later A/B hypothesis.

body.reflection: This checkpoint continues the same 42-minute PPO run with unchanged hardware and reward. At 36,579,812 new interactions, it qualified for 57/64 lifts, zero turns, and no complete successes on the same exact nominal CPU starts. Two episodes violated the finger travel allowance and there were no stops. Final robot rest was 13/64. Keep the r0045 incumbent for target R2 and continue the already planned run. Separate diagnostics found that the 24.56M checkpoint can complete the training turn condition from the halfway state but that moving the same physically prepared state upward by 55 or 110 mm did not lower its suffix success. The missing early rotation is a more direct hypothesis than height alone.

body.text: The clearance-only diagnosis in r0048 did not hold. With the 24.56M policy I translated the 16 prepared turn pairs vertically by 55 or 110 mm, preserved their relative grasp and stationary joint targets, and re-solved the published arm IK. All resets were reachable and safe by the initialization checks. Advancement was 12/16 at both heights versus 11/16 at their original height. With progress credit reset to zero on the original prepared poses, the actor still advanced on 9/16. Those states started at blade tilts of 35–78 degrees and their usual reset initialized 8.7–31 degrees of partial turn. When I rotated the same physical pairs back to blades-horizontal at equal clearance and zero credit, 6 of 16 positions were no longer reachable within the pose and stop limits. On the ten paired reachable tests the original poses advanced 5/10 and the horizontal poses 2/10. This supports filling the curriculum gap immediately after a horizontal lift, using reachable physically settled grasps from zero partial turn. Preserve the reward and final policy action map in the first controlled curriculum change, after R2 replay and the first run endpoint. Treat the tested turn starts and their metrics as diagnostic rather than full deployment successes.

reward_terms.name: seat

reward_terms.name: reference_wrist

reward_terms.name: reference_contact
reward_terms.formula: Progress-conditioned gain in object-frame contact agreement with reconstructed witnesses within a 9 mm free band.

reward_terms.name: bonus

reward_terms.name: slip
reward_terms.formula: Negative blade-angle displacement past 0.10 degree when an opposed grip moves the object with nearly stationary finger joints.

reward_terms.name: regularity
reward_terms.formula: Negative mean absolute target change, metres and radians.

body.reflection: At 48,989,446 new PPO transitions, ordered fixed-start lift improved to 61/64 and turn appeared on 5/64. Four turned starts had no hardware violation. Two trials overall had finger excursions of 0.02043 and 0.02055 rad, with zero stops, zero carry or place, and 13 final rests. Relative blade rotation at the five measured turns was 62.7 to 95.8 degrees. All five reached blade tilt at most 25 degrees with an invalid object estimate and thumb plus middle-finger contact. They lost unsupported contact 0.14 to 0.29 seconds after the first upright sample, still 103 to 173 mm outside the goal rectangle. For seed 967882 the object reached 18.8 degrees world tilt and 75.6 degrees opposed blade rotation under the local stage check. Deployment package contract passed at 0.268 ms p99. This is the original scheduled run with unchanged settings. Continue to the endpoint before choosing the next gate. The new turns are evidence against a hard observation barrier. Re-registering the occluded pose estimator at lift in a separate diagnostic gave 1/24 turns for the 24.56M checkpoint versus 0/24 unmodified. A visibility intervention with ordinary reacquisition also gave 0/24.

body.text: r0051 changes the diagnosis at the 48.99M checkpoint. The same PPO run now meets the complete turn criteria in 5/64 fixed starts, four without hardware violations. We opened seed 967882 and saw the housing turn in the thumb and middle/ring grip, then lose contact before the carry. Across those five starts, the plug was still 103–173 mm from the goal rectangle and lost unsupported contact within 0.14–0.29 s of becoming upright. The estimator was invalid for all five turns. In a separate same-seed intervention at 24.56M, increasing visibility after lift with ordinary reacquisition changed 0/24 turns to 0/24 and immediate test-only registration changed it to 1/24. This supports giving the existing reward and PPO lineage more experience. Before the next long block, correct the training horizon: the earlier run length was logged, but it used 340 policy steps on most deployment starts, 900 on a periodic subset, and 185 in reset exercises. The learning document calls for the 900-step episode. Keep all non-stopped training starts live for that full horizon in the next block. Complete the R2 judgment and replay before implementing a repair.

The plug lies outside the goal in the later views. Final palm and finger ranges were 8.5 mm and 0.127 rad, and ring MCP2 exceeded its limit by 0.061 rad.

Estimator loss covers policy time 0.50–2.67 s. The plug ends at median x = 0.636 m, y = 0.014 m and blade tilt 90.2 degrees. Ring MCP2 exceeded its limit by 0.089 rad.
